source: Table ids, names and encounter types from rejuv-map-encounters.generated.json (the tables the game reads, Data/maps.dat); the map tree from rejuv-item-events.generated.json; the order areas open in from BIGJRA's walkthrough (bigjra.github.io/rejuvenation, game 14.0.28, chapters 1 to 16 on the Paragon route; its Renegade chapter 16 is not written). Checked against the V14.0 install: field-move badges (HM_TO_BADGE in Scripts/Rejuv/Settings.rb), terrain tags, rock and tree events, transfers and event page conditions in the map files, and the events that award badges.
convention: Per encounter type, the badges actually held when that table can first be met; null = cannot be met (the map has no tile or event that sets the table off, or the map is never entered). Where only the walkthrough chapter is known, the count at its start; inside a chapter the count held at that point: Route 1, Goldenwood Forest and Goldenwood Cave follow the first gym (1), the Darchlight Manor follows the Rose Badge (10), chapter 15's last quests follow the Forgery Badge (15), and chapter 16 runs 15 until the Oblitus gym, 17 after it (both Fairy Tale badges are awarded together) and 18 after the Sigil Pearl. A field-move table is the later of its area and the move. Floria and Terajuma are closed from the Grand Express in chapter 10 until Fly, so anything there that needs 10 or 11 badges is 12. Never earlier than certain: where the evidence leaves two badges open, the later one, and the note says so. reach is the badge count at which the player first sets foot on the map, whatever its tables need; null for a map never entered in normal play, which also covers the maps filed beneath it in the map tree that have no record of their own. Normal play is a first playthrough on the Paragon route: maps entered only on the Renegade route, in New Game+, by password or in the Xenpurgis tower are null. A map named REMOVED is dated when the story still sends the player there, and its note says what leads there. An entry with empty types dates a map that has no table: one that holds shops or gifts, or one the map tree files under a place of a different badge. oneTime marks a map the player passes through once and cannot return to; a map that closes late (Grand Dream City, when chapter 16 begins) is not one-time and its note says when it closes.
